event.summary: Qualify the catch-up test’s all-frames-applied rationale
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: the rewritten takeover-test explanation says all received grid frames have been applied and are ready to reveal, although history can still be queued when this test’s reveal occurs. Future readers get an incorrect synchronization guarantee. Details: grid-attach.spec.ts:433–435 newly adds the inference "The grid applies frames as they arrive, so they are all there to reveal." openCatchUp at :422–426 only sends attach.jsonl and checks hidden/unrevealed. The fixture contains two history messages with two rows each. grid-terminal.js:1973–1994 queues model history, gives a no-backlog arrival one bounded slice, and schedules remaining work; :1886–1918 applies later slices by animation frame/task. grid-model.js:971–1005 checks its yield predicate after every row, so even this small fixture has no source guarantee that both rows finish before a yield. terminal.js:3774–3778 expressly says history may still be applying and reveals the current screen via scrollToBottom/flush; grid-terminal.js:1997–2000 flush only paints and does not drain history. The actual test at grid-attach.spec.ts:442–450 waits for revealed, checks the detach banner and visible first screen row, and never asserts drained history. Its executable screen/reveal checks remain useful and are not claimed broken. Governing contract: SPEC_impl.md, The grid client, says history is applied "in slices between frames so that the screen stays usable"; the reveal implementation’s explicit caveat agrees. Fix the rationale to say the current screen is applied and can be revealed while received history may still be pending; do not add a history wait unless a caller truly needs that boundary. Range attribution: compared f560058 parent lines738–745, which says the grid applies frames as they arrive but does not add the new all-there-to-reveal inference; the complete base-to-tip diff retains that newly added sentence. Therefore this is a changed documentation claim, not a new history-loss or test-oracle behavior regression. Suggested bucket: other, test synchronization documentation. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract analysis only; no runtime behavior observed. proposed_drop:false. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. possible_cover: caller-supplied g181/c2 is the same underlying applied-history-versus-marker distinction in a different test helper, so consolidation may be appropriate; no prohibited coverage sources searched. Caveats: ordinary tiny fixture drains likely finish immediately; timing likelihood does not establish the unconditional explanation. No reproduction, test, build or live-install action performed. Original lead consequence narrowed to the false documentation inference; fixture/caller/flush/yield premises are now checked, with no unresolved premise.
